summary: Duplicate function executions when Go http.Client cookie-jar + auth refresh rotate idempotency salt on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool/function executions (webhook calls and downstream jobs) after a transient network reconnect during long-lived streaming requests. The client is a Go microservice using net/http.Client with a shared cookie jar + a local retry middleware that refreshes OAuth tokens mid-stream.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate side effects in customer systems (duplicate database writes, duplicate webhook deliveries).
- Appears intermittently under load and on auth token refresh windows; impacts business-critical pipelines for Nimble Insights.

Environment:
- Customer using Redwood Dedicated pool in us-east, SDK: redwood-go v0.14.2 with custom retry middleware.
- Request pattern: streaming chat with function calling enabled; each function invocation includes an idempotency salt generated client-side per-request.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long-running stream request that triggers a function call (func_call).
2) While stream is inflight, trigger OAuth refresh (short-lived tokens) — middleware reissues Authorization header and rotates the per-request idempotency salt (client code currently ties salt to current auth token timestamp).
3) Net/http client reconnects (underlying TCP reset) and retry middleware replays the request with the new Authorization and new salt.
4) Redwood shows two distinct function executions (server-side ids differ) and downstream webhook receives duplicate invocations.

Customer repro snippet (Go, simplified):
- key lines: cookie jar shared across goroutines, retry middleware that recalculates idempotency salt from time.Now()+token.IssuedAt.

Logs/Errors from customer side:
- service logs show same user flow id but two distinct function execution IDs returned by Redwood: func_exec_id=fe12a3 and func_exec_id=fe12b8
- webhook responses: 200 OK for both deliveries (no retries from customer).

Why this looks like an idempotency mismatch:
- Server sees a different idempotency key because the client rotated the salt mid-retry, so dedupe check misses the duplicate.
- Shared cookie jar and auth refresh cause a replay of the same logical user session but with different request metadata.

Requested from customer: guidance and a mitigation path (preferably server-side option to dedupe across acceptable salt rotations or advice for SDK patterns).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Avery Chen (Support): Initial triage - reproduced a minimal repro with customer pattern in staging; confirmed duplicate func_exec IDs when client rotates salt mid-request.

2026-03-10 13:44 - Diego Morales (SRE): Captured server logs for the replay window. Noticed that api-gateway accepts both attempts because Authorization header changed and client IP stayed same. No immediate 409 dedupe seen.

2026-03-11 08:03 - Maya Singh (SDK Team): Added hypothesis: SDK should recommend idempotency salt be independent of auth token lifecycle. Filed quick docs patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/221.
2026-03-11 12:25 - Customer (Nimble Insights): Confirmed they cannot easily decouple salt from token without refactor; requested server-side mitigation during token refresh windows.
2026-03-12 10:02 - Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced variant in TS environment using service-worker reconnect; indicates cross-SDK manifestation under similar token-rotation patterns.
investigation_notes: Checked api-gateway middleware: dedupe key currently computed from (client-id + idempotency-salt + request-path). When salt differs, dedupe bypasses.
Cookie-jar behavior: shared jar causes session cookie to persist across retries; auth header refresh changes bearer token but not session cookie.
Hypothesis A: Clients tying idempotency salt to auth token lifetime cause semantically identical requests to appear distinct when token is rotated mid-retry.
Hypothesis B: Gateway treats Authorization header change as a new principal; dedupe is conservative and avoids cross-principal dedupe to prevent security issues.
Tested temporary server tweak in staging to relax principal check for short replay window (30s) and observed correct dedupe for our repro.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps:
1) Immediate customer workaround: patch SDK usage to generate idempotency salt per logical session/request and not bind to token issuance (example guidance added to docs PR). If using Go, ensure salt is stable across retries: generate once before sending and cache for retry attempts.
2) Short-term server mitigation: implement optional gateway config flag 'accept-replay-cross-auth-delta-window' (30s) for Dedicated customers to dedupe requests that only differ by Authorization header but share session attributes. Deployed to staging for Nimble repro — reduced duplicates.
3) Long-term: SDKs will receive guidance and a helper to produce stable idempotency keys across retries; product task opened to evaluate server-side safe relaxations for dedupe across auth rotation windows.

Follow-up items:
- SDK Team to publish sample patterns and add helper in go-sdk v0.15.0 (tracking PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/1498).
- Product to approve dedicated-gateway config option and define conservative defaults.
- Security to review auth-window dedupe behavior for potential impersonation risks.

Status: in-progress; customer accepted the short-term workaround and requested ETA for SDK helper.
